message.content: The key analysis: `order` maps logical row → physical row. `_reorder` composes correctly (`next[i] = order[P[i]]`), but `_append` (lines 20–26) loads `Delta[Order[row]]` and adds it to `Cache[row]`, i.e., it uses the inverse permutation direction — the correct lazy append is `Cache[Order[row]] += Delta[row]`. These coincide only when `Order` is an involution. Each individual `P[k]` is an involution, but a word like `(0,1,2)` makes `Order = P1∘P0`, which is generally not an involution — exactly the case the smoke words never exercise. Recording the description model now.

message.reasoning_content:
Analyze semantics. Lazy representation: order maps logical row -> physical row? Check.

order initially identity. _reorder: next[i] = order[P[i]]. If logical row i currently maps to physical order[i], after logical perm C_next = C[P], logical row i of new = logical row P[i] of old = physical order[P[i]]. Correct.

_append: cache[physical r] += Delta[source=?]. It loads source = Order + row (physical row index?), then Cache[row] += Delta[source]. Hmm. _append adds Delta at index source = Order[row] — but row here indexes physical rows (0..N-1). Delta addresses CURRENT LOGICAL rows. Logical row j has physical row Order[j]. To add Delta[j] to physical slot Order[j]. In _append, iteration row over 0..N-1 as physical: source = Order[row] — wrong direction? Correct would be for logical j: cache[Order[j]] += Delta[j], i.e., store to Order[row] and load Delta[row]. The kernel loads Delta[Order[row]] and stores to Cache[row]. Since Order is a permutation, Cache[row] += Delta[Order[row]] means physical row row gets Delta of logical row j where Order[j]=row, i.e., inverse mapping. That's wrong unless Order is an involution. Each P is an involution, and reorders compose: Order = P_k∘...? next[i]=order[P[i]] = order∘P. Composition of involutions is not an involution generally. So words like (0,1) give a non-involution order, and _append applies Delta at inverse-permuted rows — a real bug surface.

Materialize: Output[row] = Cache[Order[row]] — logical row row = physical Order[row]. Consistent with order = logical->physical.

So risk: _append uses Delta[Order[row]] added to Cache[row]; correct requires Delta[row] added to Cache[Order[row]]. Equivalent only when Order is an involution (Order == Order^{-1}). Words with alternating two different permutations likely fail. Smoke tests all kept order involutive (0,0 / 1,1) or single reorder. Words like (0,1,2) — run default! — order = P1∘P0 likely non-involution.
